# Air pump and vacuum experiments (`air_pump_vacuum`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/physics.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Physics, optics & astronomy (`physics`)
- Deps: needs piston_pump; helped by atmospheric_pressure, boring_machine, glassmaking
- Core idea: A piston pump with two valves, turned round so that it draws air out of a closed vessel instead of water out of a well. Each stroke removes a fraction of what is left. Everything depends on tightness: a truly round barrel, a leather piston soaked in oil, joints sealed with wax or kept under water, a tap between pump and vessel. In the emptied glass a candle goes out, a bell can hardly be heard, warm water boils, and a feather falls as fast as a coin. Two close-fitting copper bowls emptied of air cannot be pulled apart by teams of horses. Much later the same art gives light bulbs and electron tubes.
- Pitfalls:
  - Expecting a perfect vacuum; early pumps reached perhaps a tenth to a hundredth of an atmosphere
  - Thin or flat-sided glass vessels implode; use thick round ones
  - Leaks at every joint; without constant sealing nothing works, as Boyle's critics found
- History: europe: c. 1647–1650 Guericke's first pump; 1654 Regensburg and 1657 Magdeburg hemisphere shows; 1659 Boyle and Hooke's pump with glass receiver; 1705 Hauksbee's double-barrel pump; 1855 Geissler and 1865 Sprengel mercury pumps; china: double-acting piston bellows long in use, but no evacuation pump before European contact
- Read:
  - Robert Boyle, New Experiments Physico-Mechanicall, Touching the Spring of the Air (1660)
  - Steven Shapin & Simon Schaffer, Leviathan and the Air-Pump (1985)
